title: Proof Protocol
concept: Proof is a specific change, evidence you can both see, and a set time window. A promise without those is just hope.
whenToUse: After any real request for change; whenever “I promise” shows up with no plan behind it; instead of waiting for things to get better.
steps: Name the change — something specific you can both see.
Decide what counts — agree what ‘met’, ‘partial’ and ‘missed’ will look like.
Set a time window — start date, end date, and when you’ll check in.
Keep the record short — a count or a table — and look at it together at the check-in, where feelings and questions come first.
Check in — extend it, adjust it, or close it out, together.
Missed twice and nobody’s said so? Raise it at the next check-in.

phrases.text: I need proof, not a promise. The change: ___. Evidence: ___. Window: ___. Check-in: ___.
I’m committing to ___, visible as ___, through ___.
At check-in: how are we each feeling? Then let’s look at the record together.

working: After rows, A has been going quiet with no return time. The change: every Pause + Return gets an exact return time. Each return is noted, kept or not; they look at it together at the 14-day check-in. Six of six kept. B says the evenings feel less tense.
notWorking: “I’ll be better at communicating.” There’s no specific behaviour, nothing either of you can check and no time window, so nothing changes.
activity: Write one Proof item today on a sticky note: Behaviour / Evidence / Window / Review. Both initial.
